title: Supernova
body:
A **supernova** is the explosion ending a massive star's life, briefly outshining the entire
galaxy around it. Two mechanisms produce one.

**Core collapse**, in a star above about 8 solar masses. Such a star fuses progressively
heavier elements in shells around its core, each stage shorter than the last, until the core is
iron. Fusing iron absorbs energy where every earlier stage released it, so the outward pressure
disappears and the core collapses in under a second. The infalling outer layers rebound off the
collapsed core and are blown away.

**Type Ia**, in a [[Binary Stars|binary]] system, where a [[White Dwarf]] accretes
matter from its companion until it crosses the Chandrasekhar limit and detonates. Because the
trigger is always the same mass, the energy released is always about the same, which makes it a
standard candle for the [[Inverse-Square Law]].

The consequences reach past the star:

```
element production   everything heavier than iron forms during and after the explosion
enrichment           the debris seeds the interstellar medium for the next generation
remnant              a Neutron Star below ~3 solar masses, a Black Hole above
shock waves          compress nearby clouds and trigger Star Formation
```

The first line is the one to keep. The iron in blood and the calcium in bone were produced in a
star and scattered by an explosion, which is the sense in which the material of the Earth is
second-hand stellar debris.
